$description: The pane's own chrome — the pane context bar, one mount per pane. (The floating zoom pod that used to ride with it is the status bar's zoom field now: `surfaces/statusbar.json`.) It replaces `#tab-bar`, a 28px band styled identically to the tab strip above it that held five unrelated axes with no labels on any of them; the three axes here each say what they are, and the label is what stops the band re-accreting into an anonymous strip of chips. `panels/pane-context.ts` keeps every decision — which editor kinds a document declares, which canvas views it has, what a lens may not write, and what a route param's candidate values are — and hands this document one projection of words, booleans and keyed rows. The bar and the banner share `[part="band"]` so the adapter can MEASURE what the stage must clear: a banner's height is its wrapped text, and only layout knows how many lines that is.

style.$description: The `.pc-*` rules of `styles/canvas.css`, keyed on `part` and carried here, plus `.jx-collab-banner` from `styles/shell.css` — the banner rides in this band and the rule rides with it. Three token repairs travel with them, all of one shape: `--spectrum-font-size-75` and `--spectrum-font-size-50` resolved only inside `<sp-theme>` and a document mounts outside it, so every rule reading one would silently have taken its px fallback; they are `--jx-text-md` (12px) and `--jx-text-sm` (11px) here, at the same values. Rules are DELETED rather than moved where the kit already draws them: `.pc-derive-trigger`'s hand-built 22×20 box and its hover are `jx-action-button` quiet, and `.pc-ctx-manage:hover`'s underline is the only half of that rule worth keeping. The one rule ADDED is `pointer-events: auto` on the band and the popovers: `.pane-chrome` is `pointer-events: none` and gave it to its direct children through `.pane-chrome > *`, which a document root with `display: contents` is not — so the two surfaces that take the pointer say so themselves, which is also the honest place for it.

& [part=\"band\"].$description: The pane's top band: the bar plus the standing statements that must be readable before the first keystroke. One element so the adapter can MEASURE what the stage has to clear — a banner's height is its wrapped text, which only layout knows.

& [part=\"spacer\"].$description: What pushes the other axes right, and where Back, the Editor axis and §18.4's preset trigger go. It stays in a lens, which draws no trigger: dropping it would move the one control a lens does draw. It grows but never shrinks below what it holds: at `min-width: 0` a narrow pane squeezed it under its own Editor segments, which then painted over the View and Context axes; now the bar's `overflow: hidden` clips at the trailing end instead.

& [part=\"axis-label\"].$description: The label is the point: five unlabelled controls on a 28px band is what this replaces, and the name is what stops the band re-accreting into an anonymous strip of chips.

& [part=\"editor-kind\"].$description: A segmented strip that holds its width: the spacer it sits in is what gives way.

& [part=\"banner\"].$description: A standing statement, not an after-the-fact refusal: a guest without write access used to watch their edits apply locally and vanish at the publish gate. Inside the band the stage is offset by, so it pushes the document down instead of covering the one it is warning about.

& [part=\"popover\"].$description: Both panels take the pointer that `.pane-chrome` withholds. A popover is in the top layer while it shows, which changes where it PAINTS and not where it is in the tree, so it inherits `pointer-events: none` from the chrome layer exactly as the band does.

& [part=\"ctx\"].$description: One column of labelled groups over a footer that leaves for the definition site. This control only SELECTS; the definitions live in Project Settings › Contexts (§6.2), and nothing in it defines a breakpoint, a scheme or a feature query.

& [part=\"features\"].$description: The group that WRAPS, and the reason it is not a segmented control. A feature list is as long as the project makes it and this popover is a 240–340px column, so it folds onto a second line in any project with more than a few; a compact group cannot draw that — its seam is written in tree order, no selector can find the ends of a flex line, and it therefore refuses to wrap and would overflow the column instead (ui.md §5.4). Chips instead: each member draws its own rounded frame (`quiet: false`, since the group no longer frames it) and the chosen one takes the accent edge below. The gap is --jx-space-2 rather than the group's own 2px, which puts every small chip's hit area at the 24px floor on both axes instead of the 22px two overlapping extensions leave (§4.3). The size list used to wrap here beside it; it is a segmented group on the bar now, which clips at its trailing end rather than wrapping.

& [part=\"features-item\"][data-selected.$description: A chosen chip reads the way a chosen segment does: the accent tint with an accent EDGE. A member's own selected state is a 15% tint over its neutral border, which among framed neighbours reads as a faint wash rather than as the one that is on — the measurement that gave the compact group its selected rule, restated here at the one place the group does not draw it. (0,4,0) over the member's own (0,3,0).

& [part=\"fields\"].$description: The fields, stacked. They were a row on the bar capped at 140px; in the popover each takes the full column so a route value or a JSON test prop is readable while you type it.

& [part=\"sizes\"], & [part=\"schemes\"].$description: Segmented strips that hold their width; the bar clips at its trailing end rather than squeezing a segment.

children.$description: Back to the workspace home, in a workspace that draws no tab strip (Media, Styles, Publish): the way out of a view opened beside the home — a media file, a comparison, `project.json` as Code — with the destination named, because there is no chip to click and no close button to press. It leads the bar so it sits where the strip's chips would have been. Escape runs the same command (`pane.backToHome`) wherever no text field or code editor owns the key.

The Editor axis leads the bar, beside Back: which editor the document is open in is the first thing the pane says about it, and the axes to its right describe that editor. Drawn only in the full bar (`hidden` in a lens, whose tab is the pane beside it). Several declared kinds are a segmented `jx-action-group`, like the View axis: they are few, and every one of them stays on screen rather than behind a dropdown.
